findings.conditions: updatefaceElemMatrix: owner of a shared face is still in its receive loop when another rank, finished with the call, sends any further message on mpiComm_ (or one is still pending)
findings.reasoning: The owners of shared faces receive with MPI_ANY_SOURCE and MPI_ANY_TAG and use Status.MPI_TAG as the face global ID (BinarySearch in faceList). The face sends are fire-and-forget Isends (request overwritten, never waited), and there is no synchronisation after the loop, only a Barrier at entry. A fast rank that leaves and sends anything else on mpiComm_ can have that message taken in place of a face message. BinarySearch then returns -1 and cols[-1]/ncols[-1] are indexed (crash), or, if the tag happens to equal a face ID, foreign data is merged into the wrong face (wrong result). The real face message is left unreceived and steals a later receive. Which message is taken depends on arrival order.

findings.conditions: hypre_SetUpFactor with neighbour cycles (P sends to Q and Q to P) and an MPI that does not buffer the rnum messages (synchronous mode or nlevels above the eager limit)
findings.reasoning: Every rank first does blocking MPI_Send of rnum (nlevels ints) to all spes[i], and only afterwards posts the blocking MPI_Recv from rpes[i]. No receive is pre-posted for TAG_SetUp_rnum. With a symmetric communication pattern each pair of neighbours sends to each other first. If the sends are not buffered (large nlevels so the message goes rendezvous, or Ssend semantics), all ranks block in MPI_Send and the program deadlocks. Whether it completes depends only on MPI buffering. The other pilut exchanges pre-post Irecv before their blocking sends; this one does not.

findings.conditions: HYPRE_LSI_MLConstructMHMatrix with mutual neighbours and unbuffered (synchronous) sends
findings.reasoning: Every rank does blocking MPI_Send of its receive lengths (msgid 539) to all recvProc[i] before posting any receive; the matching MPI_Recv with MPI_ANY_SOURCE comes only afterwards. In a symmetric pattern every rank blocks in MPI_Send waiting for a receive that the peer has not posted, so progress relies on the MPI buffering the 1-int message eagerly. Under synchronous or zero-buffer semantics this deadlocks. The ANY_SOURCE receive itself correctly records status.MPI_SOURCE, so only the buffering dependence is a bug.

findings.conditions: MH matrix construction for Maxwell with mutual neighbours and unbuffered sends
findings.reasoning: This is the same pattern as HYPRE_LSI_ml.c: blocking MPI_Send of lengths (msgid 539) to all recvProc before the MPI_ANY_SOURCE MPI_Recv loop, with no pre-posted receive. Completion depends on eager buffering of the send; with synchronous-mode sends, neighbours that send to each other deadlock.

findings.conditions: two hypre_LocateAssumedPartition calls on the same communicator with no intervening synchronisation (tag 17 reused); a fast rank's second-call message overtakes a slow third rank's first-call message
findings.reasoning: The loop receives MPI_ANY_SOURCE, tag 17, until rows_found == locate_row_count, and records status.MPI_SOURCE plus the range. If a later Locate (another matrix or vector on the same comm) sends tag-17 messages before this rank has finished, a foreign range can be counted. The partition then gets a wrong owner or range, or rows_found can overshoot (the != test then hangs), and the stolen message is missing from the next call. In current callers a DataExchangeList (a global termination tree) usually follows each Locate, which makes this unlikely.
